answer: A graduated bond ladder resists sybil farms: every identity locks capital that a detected clone forfeits. Registration stakes a bond pegged to the median revenue horizon; the first terrace is cheap, but each added identity per cluster pays double the prior tier, so 100 clones cost ~2^99 times the base bond. Basalt-hard checkpoints hash attestation graphs and timing fingerprints per epoch, and one confirmed cluster slashes the terrace. Honest agents amortize one bond across thousands of tasks; attackers face a cost curve that outruns revenue before detection.
